fatal_errors: The proposed CrN film does not reconstruct the target FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on Cu.
The PVD intervention is unrelated to the target temperature-dependent nanoindentation and friction simulations.
None of the cited evidence supports CrN deposition on Cu, CrN-Cu adhesion, or the claimed performance improvements.
The asserted 20% and 30% improvements, sub-1-um thickness boundary, and falsification thresholds are unsupported.
The hypothesis omits the critical 900 K transition, lattice disorder, dislocation evolution, HCP fraction, and temperature-dependent friction response.
explanation: The answer addresses surface protection of Cu only at a generic level. It substitutes a conventional CrN coating for the target FCC FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating and fails to reproduce the simulated loading protocol, temperature range, structural mediators, or the sharp degradation above 900 K. Its scratch and wear tests could provide limited empirical discrimination for a CrN coating, but they do not directly measure adhesion and use arbitrary thresholds. The cited papers discuss high-entropy alloys generally and provide no valid support for the proposed CrN/Cu system or its quantitative claims.
